newsitem.title: USA: Jewish group urges law firm to aid Holocaust charity.
newsitem.headline: Jewish group urges law firm to aid Holocaust charity.

text.p: A Jewish group called on Tuesday on a prestigious New York law firm to donate fees it receives for representing Credit Suisse, a major Swiss bank under scrutiny for its wartime activities, to a charity to aid Holocaust victims.

"They should donate the millions of dollars in fees they are receiving to the newly created fund to aid Holocaust victims," World Jewish Congress executive director Elan Steinberg said of the decision by Cravatt Swaine & Moore to represent the bank.
"That would demonstrate that their decision to represent Credit Suisse came from a pure and alturistic motive," he added.

The law firm's decision to represent Credit Suisse provoked a fierce internal debate, with some partners objecting to taking on a client that allegedly helped the Nazis finance their war effort by laundering money for the Third Reich.
Several of the law firm's partners and associates are active in Jewish causes.

Credit Suisse was one of three major Swiss banks that recently donated $68 million to help start a fund to aid Holocaust victims that will be jointly administered by Swiss government appointees and persons appointed by Jewish groups.
